claim: For every integer \(n\ge4\), let \(A\) be a binary \(3\times n\) ecological incidence matrix containing exactly \(n+2\) ones, with no zero row and no zero column. Let classical normalized NODF sum, over all unordered unequal-degree row pairs and unordered unequal-degree column pairs, their neighborhood overlap divided by the smaller positive degree, and divide this score by \(K=\binom n2+3\). Then \[\max_A\mathrm{NODF}(A)=\frac{2n-2}{\binom n2+3}.\] Equality holds if and only if, up to permutations of rows and columns, the incidence matrix has one row containing all \(n\) ones and two single-one rows using two distinct columns: \[A_n=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1&\cdots&1\\1&0&0&\cdots&0\\0&1&0&\cdots&0\end{pmatrix}.\] There are exactly \(3n(n-1)\) labeled maximizers, constituting one unlabeled isomorphism type; all maximizing bipartite graphs are connected trees. Every Ferrers (perfectly nested-neighborhood) matrix satisfying the same census and no-isolate constraints instead has NODF \((n+1)/K\); thus its ceiling is lower by exactly \((n-3)/K\). The surprising conclusion is that two mutually incomparable specialist neighborhoods are required by every optimal sparse network, despite optimizing a measure named nestedness. The result concerns classical equal-weight row/column NODF with unequal-degree comparisons only, and its link constraint is essential.
integrity: The proof splits the forced degree-excess equation \(\sum_j(d(c_j)-1)=2\) into exhaustive cases and reconstructs all equality conditions. A standalone exact rational verifier independently checks all 63,906 admissible matrices in the dimensions \(3\times2\) through \(3\times7\) with two distinct scoring implementations. Finite checking is supportive only; the structural proof covers arbitrary \(n\ge4\).
scientific_limitations: This is a binary fixed-link NODF optimization theorem for exactly three species in one guild and \(n\ge4\) in the other, with \(n+2\) interactions and no isolated vertices. It uses pairwise unequal-fill normalized overlap and is not a claim about all nestedness indices, weights, fixed degree sequences, denser networks, or causal ecology.
title: A sharp sparse-link NODF bound forces incomparable specialists
